name: Mediatore
description: Mediatore is an Italian trick-taking game for four players, closely related to Tressette. It features a unique bidding system where the final bidder plays alone against a team of three, or chooses a partner by calling a card. The game uses a 40-card Italian deck and includes a 'monte' of undealt cards that can improve the bidder's hand.

history.origins: Mediatore is a variant of Tressette, one of Italy's most popular card games. It developed as a way to add bidding complexity to the base game, allowing for more strategic depth.
timeline: Traditional: Evolved from Tressette in Italian card-playing circles
20th Century: Rules formalized in Italian game collections
Present: Played in Italy, particularly in regions where Tressette is popular
history.cultural: A game for serious card players in Italy, often played in social clubs and family gatherings. The bidding adds a poker-like element to the traditional trick-taking format.
history.evolution: The key innovation of Mediatore is the bidding system that creates variable partnerships, unlike the fixed partnerships in standard Tressette.

setup.players: 4 players, playing individually or in variable partnerships based on bidding.
setup.deck: 40-card Italian deck (or standard deck minus 8s, 9s, 10s). Suits: Coins, Cups, Swords, Clubs. Ranking: 3 (high), 2, Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 7, 6, 5, 4 (low).
setup.dealing: 9 cards to each player in batches of 3. The remaining 4 cards form the 'monte' (talon) placed face down.
setup.equipment: 40-card Italian deck or modified standard deck.

rules.objective: Win the majority of the 11 card points available in tricks. The team or player who bid must make their contract.
rules.gameplay: Play follows Tressette rules: must follow suit if possible, highest card of led suit wins the trick. The 3 is the highest card in each suit.
keyRules: 3 is the highest card in each suit
Bidder may exchange with the monte (in most bids)
Partner is determined by called card in 'Chiamo'
Need majority of 11 points to win

strategy.basic: Remember the unusual card ranking (3-2-Ace are high). Try to capture 3s, 2s, and Aces. In bidding, only bid if you have strong cards.
strategy.intermediate: When calling a partner, call a card you don't have but suspect an opponent might. Use the monte exchange to improve your hand composition. Try to deduce who your partner is from their plays.
strategy.advanced: Card counting is essential - track all 3s, 2s, and Aces. As the secret partner, give subtle signals through your card play. Time your high cards to win critical tricks.
tips: The 3s are the most valuable cards - save them for important tricks
If you have multiple Aces, consider calling one you don't have to confuse opponents
Watch which cards opponents play to deduce the secret partnership
In Mediatore bid, the monte exchange can dramatically improve your hand

scoring.description: Points are awarded based on the bid and whether the contract was made. Higher bids score more but are harder to make.
scoring.winCondition: Win at least 6 of the 11 available points in tricks.
